answer: Registration requires k witnesses in distinct network regions to echo a nonce back within tight latency bounds, and the verifier tests pairwise round-trip times against the triangle inequality. A single datacenter cluster can fake geography, but its timings collapse onto one hub, leaving a visible plume of near-identical measurements; every witness bond, saffron-tagged at post, is then burned. Faking k identities costs real hosts in k regions plus k forfeitable bonds, well above one identity's yield.
